summary: Premium B2B corporate website for HERBOTECH HERBAL PVT. LTD. showcasing herbal raw-material processing, quality assurance, infrastructure, and a lead‑generation enquiry system.
requirements: Home page with hero, intro, capabilities, product portfolio, quality philosophy, workflow, infrastructure, differentiation, industries served, partnership CTA.
About Us page with vision, mission, philosophy, regional focus.
Products page with catalogue grid, search/filter, per‑herb enquiry, expandable detail view.
Processing Capabilities page detailing each unit operation with equipment photos and purpose.
Quality Assurance page explaining tests, COA demo, batch traceability.
Infrastructure page showing facility layout, storage, processing, drying, lab, packaging.
Sustainability page outlining responsible sourcing and efficiency measures.
Contact Us page with location map and a detailed Request a Quote form (name, company, email, phone, industry, herb, form, quantity, specs, message).
Form includes client‑side validation, loading/spam‑honeypot states, success/error feedback.
Form submission POSTs to /api/enquiry; on load the app GETs /api/health to confirm API reachability.
Reusable UI kit (Button, Input, Card, Modal, Layout) styled with Tailwind, using Playfair Display/Inter typography and prescribed colour palette.
Sticky header with logo, nav links, prominent CTA; mobile drawer navigation.
Consistent footer with quick links, services, social placeholders.
SEO: page titles, meta descriptions, Open Graph, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, semantic HTML.
Performance: optimized images, lazy‑load, minimal JS/CSS, Vercel‑ready build.
Accessibility: WCAG AA contrast, keyboard navigable forms, ARIA labels, focus traps.
Animations via Framer Motion: page transitions, hero parallax, scroll reveals, hover effects, smooth button interactions.
No fake certifications, testimonials, or unverified operational claims.
Deployable on Vercel with environment variable placeholders for future Supabase/API keys.
assumptions: Frontend built with Next.js 13+ App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide icons.
Backend built with FastAPI, Python 3.11, SQLAlchemy ORM, SQLite database for enquiry storage.
No actual Supabase credentials provided; backend stores enquiries locally; frontend ready to swap to Supabase later.
High‑resolution images will be supplied later; placeholders used with descriptive alt text.
Contact form does not integrate with real email/SMS; success message indicates receipt.
No multi‑language or user authentication required.
Site follows HTTPS; Vercel provides automatic SSL.
Analytics and third‑party scripts not required for MVP.

tasks.title: Project setup, health endpoint, enquiry DB model
tasks.description: Initialize FastAPI project, configure SQLite with SQLAlchemy, create Enquiry table (id, fullName, companyName, businessEmail, phoneNumber, industry, requiredHerb, productForm, estimatedQuantity, requiredSpecifications, additionalMessage, createdAt). Implement GET /api/health returning {status: 'ok'}. Add CORS middleware allowing Vercel domain.

GET /api/health returns 200 with JSON {status: 'ok'}

tasks.title: Implement POST /api/enquiry endpoint with validation and storage
tasks.description: Create route POST /api/enquiry accepting JSON body matching EnquiryRequest schema. Validate required fields, email format, phone length, enum values. Insert record into SQLite, return 201 with {message, enquiryId}. On validation failure return 422 with detail; on spam detection (honeypot field present) return 400. Include logging.

risks: Delay in obtaining final high‑resolution photography may force reliance on placeholders, affecting visual polish.
Over‑use of Framer Motion animations could cause layout thrash on low‑end devices if not moderated.
Form spam protection relies on honeypot and basic validation; determined bots may still submit unwanted entries.
Accessibility oversights in custom modal focus trapping or missing ARIA labels could exclude keyboard users.
SEO metadata may be omitted inadvertently on dynamically generated pages (e.g., product detail).
Vercel deployment could fail if environment variables are missing or if Next.js config incompatible with selected runtime.
Future migration to Supabase will require adapting data layer if the backend is tightly coupled to SQLite.
Client‑side filtering on product catalogue may degrade performance if catalogue grows significantly; mitigation: keep data limited or implement server‑side filtering later.
Colour contrast on text over background images may fall below WCAG AA if images are not sufficiently darkened.
Learning curve of Next.js App Router may lead to mis‑routed pages or 404s during development, requiring careful testing.
